title: Catching a tampered record
story: Someone alters one Decision record in a copy of the Audit chain. Verify runs on the copy and points to exactly the record that was changed. The real records are never touched.

chat.speaker: asha
chat.text: Reorder my usual milk and bread, please.

chat.speaker: shopbot
chat.text: Your usual basket at FreshMart comes to INR 1,250. Checking with AgentPay Guard before I pay.

chat.speaker: asha
chat.text: What if someone edited that record later?

what_to_notice: Changing a single byte breaks that record's hash, so Verify names it as the first broken record. This ran on an in-memory copy: the real chain still verifies clean, and the database refuses edits outright.
